reading.section: The second limitation of leaf attachment

mathematical_checks.claim: The three original marks form a string C-group.
mathematical_checks.proof: All are distinct nonidentity involutions. a and c commute and generate V4. Put A=<a,b>, H=<b,c>, K=<a,c>. The product bc has order four, so the group of two involutions H is D8 of order eight. The orbit of {2,3} consists exactly of {2,3},{2,4},{3,5},{4,5}: closure and reachability are checked by the two displayed involutions. Its stabilizer is therefore order two and contains b, hence equals <b>. A preserves {1,2,3} and H fixes 1, so A intersect H is <b>. Independently of a retained rank-three criterion, A intersect K=<a>, because c and ac cross {1,2,3}; H intersect K=<c>, because a and ac move 1. Each two-generator group has the rank-two intersection property since its displayed involutions are distinct. These three maximal-pair equalities imply every subset intersection: embed two proper subsets in different maximal subsets, intersect first with their singleton common support, and use the rank-two identities. Equal or nested maximal supports reduce directly to rank two. Thus all rank-three subset identities hold.

Starting from c, successive conjugation by b,a,b,a,b gives edge supports 34,25,16,17,27,36. These form the spanning path 4-3-6-1-7-2-5. Tree-edge transpositions generate the full symmetric group: conjugating adjacent edge transpositions supplies the transposition between the first and last vertices of any path, and all transpositions generate S7. All six lie in <a,b,c>, proving equality rather than only an order estimate.

mathematical_checks.claim: Adding the endpoint mark x preserves the string relations but fails the intersection property.
mathematical_checks.proof: x is disjoint from b and c. Since (xa)^3=(56), <x,a> contains (56), a(56)=(12), and x=(01); these generate Sym({0,1,2}) times <(56)>. Conversely x,a lie in that direct product, giving equality. Its intersection with the original S7 fixing 0 is <(12),(56)>=C2 times C2. The common-label subgroup of {x,a} and {a,b,c} is <a>, the diagonal order-two subgroup, and is strictly smaller. This exact intersection is a proof of failure, with no search or ambient group-order computation as premise.
